name: Mbank (Al Maryah Community Bank)
founded: Incorporated as an LLC in Abu Dhabi on 6 Jun 2021 (FY2025 financial statements); CBUAE licence for 'the first all-digital bank' reported on 13 Apr 2021; first board of 11 named 14 Jun 2021. Licence number not found.
ownership_summary: Private LLC; the share register is not published. Share capital was AED 700m fully paid at 31 Dec 2025 (AED 600m at 31 Dec 2024 and AED 500m at 1 Jan 2024), the latest AED 100m increase approved by the CBUAE. The FY2025 statements, the website, the 2021 licence and board coverage and the April 2026 board announcement name no shareholders (checked 12 Oct 2026). Chairman and board are named; whether any director represents a shareholder is not stated.

shareholders.holder: Not disclosed. No shareholder names or percentages appear in the FY2023-FY2025 audited statements, the website or press coverage found.

government_link: Not found after research. No government or sovereign shareholder is disclosed. Abu Dhabi government bodies (Judicial Department, Department of Community Development, Abu Dhabi Housing Authority loan top-ups) appear as customers or partners, not as stated owners. The separate ADQ-backed digital bank mentioned in a 2021 Gulf News article is a different entity. Checked 2026-10-12.
group_structure: Group of the bank and one consolidated subsidiary: AED Stablecoin LLC - S.P.C (100%, Abu Dhabi, payment-token issuance; issuer of the AE Coin dirham stablecoin per Gulf News Feb 2026 naming the owner as Al Maryah Community Bank). Emirates Coin Investment LLC (EmCoin, 25%) was consolidated at 31 Dec 2024 and, from 1 Jan 2025, is an equity-accounted associate (carrying amount AED 10,526k; share of loss AED 1,558k); its licensed activities include portfolio and fund management and virtual-asset services. Neither is profiled separately. FY2024 statements were audited by PwC; FY2025 by EY (Abu Dhabi).

subsidiaries.name: AED Stablecoin LLC - S.P.C
subsidiaries.activity: Payment tokens issuance (AE Coin, AED-pegged stablecoin; CBUAE in-principle approval Oct 2024)

subsidiaries.name: Emirates Coin Investment L.L.C. (associate, equity method from 1 Jan 2025)
subsidiaries.activity: Licensed for portfolio management, investment fund management, virtual-asset services, arranging and advisory; crypto-settlement partner for AEC Wallet top-ups

footprint: UAE only. Head office at 454 Shakhbout Bin Sultan Street, Abu Dhabi (registered address). The Branches & ATMs page lists 21 entries (branches, ATMs and mini-branch kiosks) in Abu Dhabi, Dubai (Business Bay, Al Wasl, Mall of the Emirates ATM) and Sharjah; no total branch count is stated. A branch at Hili Mall, Al Ain opened in Nov 2025. Cash and cheque deposits through FAB's network of 396 ATMs and CDMs (Jul 2024). Checked 2026-10-12. (Sources: S13, S19, S20.)
customer_segments: Individuals (current, savings, joint, fixed-deposit and minors accounts), small businesses and corporates; Abu Dhabi Housing Authority beneficiaries (top-up loans). At 31 Dec 2025 corporate accounts were AED 4.91bn (68%) and retail accounts AED 2.34bn (32%) of customer deposits. No affluent, priority or private-banking tier found.
business_lines: Retail and corporate banking (S4 note 1). Loans at 31 Dec 2025 (gross AED 1,679.5m): corporate loans 677.7m, personal loans 465.5m, corporate overdrafts 320.4m, retail overdrafts 211.4m, credit cards 4.5m; overdrafts for share trading were AED 395.2m (corporate 191.6m, retail 203.5m). Deposits: current 2,475.1m, savings 681.3m, term 4,060.5m, cash margin 37.8m. Products on the website: Jaywan debit card, Aani instant payments, Ziyada overdraft, personal loans, insurance through Policy Bazaar, in-app IPO subscription on ADX and DFM, AEC Wallet for the AE Coin stablecoin. The largest assets are CBUAE balances (AED 2.64bn) and CBUAE monetary bills (AED 3.27bn).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Mbank is a conventional digital specialised bank serving individuals, small businesses and corporates, with no wealth, private-banking, asset-management or brokerage business found. Investment-related features are limited: in-app IPO subscription on ADX and DFM, an IPO Upgrade programme with DFM giving up to 5x subscription leverage, overdrafts for share trading (AED 395m at 31 Dec 2025), fixed deposits and insurance through Policy Bazaar. Its strategic push is the AE Coin dirham stablecoin through a 100% subsidiary (AED Stablecoin LLC) and the AEC Wallet, with a 25% associate (Emirates Coin Investment) licensed for fund management and virtual-asset services. FY2025 was the first net loss (AED 11.6m) after AED 9.7m profit in 2024, while deposits grew from AED 3.9bn to AED 7.3bn. In April 2026 the new board said it would accelerate investment in fintech and digital products and expand branches.

No in-app secondary-market trading, funds or ETFs found.

opportunities: No wealth, funds, advisory or private-banking offering found; investment features are IPO subscription and an IPO Upgrade with DFM (S9, S12).
Customers already borrow to trade shares: overdrafts for share trading were AED 395.2m at 31 Dec 2025, up from AED 282.4m a year earlier (S4 note 9).
Deposits grew from AED 3.94bn to AED 7.25bn in 2025, with AED 2.34bn from retail accounts (S4 note 17).
April 2026 board stated priorities: investment in fintech, advanced digital products and branch expansion (S18).
The 25% associate Emirates Coin Investment holds licences covering fund management and virtual-asset services, which could be a route to investment products (S4 note 13).
barriers: FY2025 net loss of AED 11.6m with operating expenses (AED 245.2m) above operating income (AED 237.8m); accumulated losses AED 118.9m (S4).
Management focus and capital are tied to the AE Coin stablecoin ecosystem (100% subsidiary, 25% associate) (S4, S22).
Most assets are CBUAE balances and M-bills (AED 5.9bn of AED 8.2bn, our calculation) and the loan book is small (AED 1.67bn net) (S4).
Mass-market and SME base with no affluent tier; board reconstituted in April 2026 (S1, S18).
Ownership undisclosed, so decision-makers behind the bank are unclear (S4).

open_items: Shareholders are not disclosed anywhere found (FY2023-FY2025 statements, website, press). The CBUAE licence register was not queried for Mbank; centralbank.ae returned 403 in the sibling ruya check (R2).

No H1 2026 or Q3 2026 financials: the IR page lists only FY2025 (approved 30 Jul 2026), FY2024, H1 2024 and FY2023 statements and Pillar 3 for 30 Jun 2024 and 31 Dec 2023. Latest period is 31 Dec 2025.
Customers, employees, AUM and wealth client assets are not disclosed.
